You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"A utility voltage sag occurred and chillers failed to restart automatically, indicating mechanical cooling may have shut down; the rule directs verifying cooling is running and treating the datacenter as on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"Mechanical cooling is down (13 chillers failed to restart) and the datacenter is running on its thermal buffer; the rule requires acting before buffer depletion and expecting automated shutdowns.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-004","because":"The control system is not mentioned as unavailable, but manual resets and manual restarts are underway, aligning with the rule's guidance to manually investigate and reset cooling equipment when visibility is limited.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S80","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]},{"rule_id":"R-008","because":"Chillers failed to restart automatically and manual restarts are being attempted; the rule warns that if chillers are bound into a cluster, individual restart will not work and configurations must be modified.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running and treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer; start planning for its depletion.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin; expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Manually investigate the affected cooling equipment and reset the affected equipment and PLCs into a maximum cooling configuration; confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down.","rule_id":"R-004"},{"action":"Check whether chillers are bound into a cluster before attempting individual restart; if bound, plan to manually modify chiller configurations to unbind them so each can be restarted individually.","rule_id":"R-008"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","reason":"Mechanical cooling is confirmed shut down (13 chillers failed to restart) and the datacenter is on a load-dependent thermal buffer; R-001 and R-002 escalation triggers are met."},"not_covered":["The specific cause of the voltage sag (e.g., storm activity) is not stated in the signals, so R-001's condition about storms being active is not confirmed.","The status of the datacenter control system (whether it is available or failed) is not provided, so R-003 and R-004's control-system conditions cannot be fully assessed.","Whether the chillers are configured as a bound cluster is not stated, so R-008's condition is not confirmed.","The current datacenter temperature and whether it is approaching safe operational thresholds is not provided, so R-002's temperature condition is not confirmed.","Whether standby chillers share a water circuit with active chillers is not stated, so R-007 cannot be applied.","Whether outside temperatures are extraordinarily high is not stated, so R-005 cannot be applied.","Whether the fire sprinkler system is at risk of activation is not stated, so R-009 cannot be applied."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Incremental load increases over time in the Availability Zone resulted in a chiller operating configuration that was susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted."},{"id":"F4","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"In this scenario, the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 11:34 UTC, as temperatures continued to increase, our onsite datacenter team began a remote shutdown of remaining networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address the thermal runaway."},{"id":"F6","kind":"response","text":"This shutdown allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed us to restart the chillers."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We have de-risked this failure to restart due to voltage fluctuations, by implementing a change to the control timing logic on the Chiller Management System (Completed)."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an ‘adjacent’ sequence to a data hall ‘load based’ sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored (Completed)."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures."},{"id":"F10","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a ‘load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed, which we have since implemented (Completed)."},{"id":"F11","kind":"impact","text":"At 10:30 UTC some networking, compute, and storage infrastructure began to shutdown automatically as data hall temperatures increased, impacting service availability."}]}
